title: Deploy shipyard: post-deploy acceptance harness for private clusters
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reusable, automated post-deploy acceptance harness ("shipyard") for Private/VPC clusters that validates API readiness, model load behavior, warmup effectiveness, and basic smoke/load safety before marking a deployment healthy. This ticket covers the terraform-coupled execution runner, check definitions, and integration with the Console alerting/playbook hooks.

Scope and deliverables:
1) A Terraform-driven hook that triggers the shipyard run automatically after successful Terraform apply for private clusters (via post-apply callback or CI job).
2) A set of declarative checks for the harness:
   - API handshake: TLS + mTLS (where configured), JWT/SSO healthcheck, SSO token exchange smoke call.
   - Routing & ingress: Verify service endpoints (internal load balancer + NAT rules) respond and return expected headers.
   - Model instantiate & readiness: Trigger a model load call that causes the serving runtime to allocate KV caches and GPU memory; assert model process reports READY via /internal/state endpoint.
   - Priming pass: Small prefix generation (configurable prompts) to create KV cache and confirm p50/p95 generation latencies improve after priming.
   - Throughput safety ramp: Incremental concurrency ramp to a configured peak (default 20 concurrent sessions) asserting <5% error rate and p95 latency SLO (default 400ms for short prompts, configurable per model).
   - Memory/FD leak check: Run short-duration sustained alloc test and assert resident memory and file descriptor counts stay within thresholds.
   - Fallback verification: Force a simulated capacity failure and assert automatic fallback to pre-configured cheaper/compact model variant works and responses are valid.
3) Failure categorization and automatic remediation suggestions: transient vs. persistent failures, and automatic retry/backoff policies with exponential delays.
4) Integration points: console/rollout API to surface check results, Slack alerting playbook link, perf dashboard link, and a PR/Concourse artifact for each run.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We will implement the shipyard runner as a small Go binary that can be invoked from CI (GitHub Actions) or via Terraform Cloud post-apply webhook. Go chosen for low runtime overhead and easy cross-compilation for on-prem deployers.
- The checks are intentionally modular and declarative (YAML check definitions) so new checks can be added by SRE or platform engineers without code changes.
- Batching & concurrency settings are model-specific; the harness will read model profiles from the existing model-catalog endpoint to pick sensible defaults.
- For customers on air-gapped installs, the runner can be executed from an operator machine; we will provide a simple container image and a CLI flag to run in offline mode.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
acceptance_criteria: Post-apply Terraform hook triggers a shipyard run and writes a structured JSON result artifact to the designated artifact store.
API handshake check validates TLS/mTLS and auth flows; failures clearly identify misconfigurations (certs vs auth).
Model instantiate check confirms model reaches READY state within configured timeout (default 180s); failures increment a metric and surface in Console.
Priming pass demonstrates improved generation latency (p95 reduction > 10%) compared to cold baseline for the same prompt set or marks test as N/A for stateless models.

Throughput ramp completes at default peak with <5% error rate and p95 < 400ms for short prompts (or configured SLO per model); if thresholds breached, the harness marks deployment UNHEALTHY and provides recommended remediation steps.
Memory and FD leak checks do not exceed configured thresholds; leaks produce a persistent failure ticket template with scraped diagnostics attached.
Fallback verification exercise succeeds for supported model variants and is recorded in the run artifact.
Console dashboard shows run results, and the rollout API can block/allow promotion of the deployment based on check outcomes.
Run artifacts include links to the GitHub PR for the Terraform change, the shipyard run logs (raw + structured JSON), and a perf snapshot uploaded to the internal dashboard.

comments: 2025-11-04 Aisha P: Ticket created. Initial scope sketched after weekly infra sync. Decided to keep checks declarative to ease future additions.
2025-11-06 Marco R: Prototype of Go runner bootstrapped. Can load YAML check bundle and execute a simple HTTP check. Pushed branch: github.com/redwood-inference/shipyard/tree/ENG-40777-proto

2025-11-08 QE: Ran the prototype against a staging private cluster. Observed model instantiate sometimes takes >180s for larger quantized models; need configurable timeout per model and a better progress probe (not just READY boolean).
2025-11-09 SRE: Agreed to add a streaming log probe that watches model stdout for LOAD_COMPLETE tokens; added to check schema as optional 'log_watch' field.
2025-11-10 Security: Confirmed KMS integration approach. Recommendation: runner should request short-lived temp creds via the control plane rather than storing keys in CI. Added security task.

2025-11-12 Marco R: Implemented priming pass and early perf snapshot upload to the internal dashboard. Ran ramp test at 15 concurrent sessions in staging; saw p95 spike to ~620ms for long-context workloads — flagged for threshold tuning. Linked perf snapshot: https://dashboards.internal.redwood/shipyard/runs/ENG-40777/20251112

2025-11-13 Aisha P: Updated acceptance criteria to allow model-specific SLOs and added playbook templates for common failures. Next: finalize Terraform hook design and prep a small canary rollout to three staging clusters.
